# Decisions: drift-hardening

- 2026-08-07T07:18:21.064Z — chose **`rule` as an optional field on decision_logged — a short imperative clause whose presence IS what makes a decision a standing constraint (one field, one concept; render contract: verbatim, never clipped, never aged out)** over a separate standing:bool flag, a new event type, or raising the existing clip budgets because C-abl (handoff-bench R04) showed decisions are the load-bearing field, and the live digest clips exactly them (over@90, decision line@280, last-5 aging). Raising budgets just moves the cliff; a new event type forks fold/render/doctor for the same semantic. An optional field keeps 0.21.0 logs valid (unknown fields already tolerated), and 'has an imperative worth verbatim rendering' is precisely the standing-constraint distinction.
- 2026-08-07T07:30:42.538Z — rule: **Never clip inside a decision rule on any surface; under budget pressure drop whole entries with a count pointer instead.** — chose **whole-entry drop with a count pointer when the standing section exceeds its budget** over clipping rule text like every other budgeted line because a clipped imperative is how dead ends recur: the operative clause is exactly what the clip cuts (observed live: scanner-version-gate rejected-approaches line truncated mid-rationale at 90 chars)
- 2026-08-07T07:58:44.675Z — rule: **A guard warns, never blocks: a guard violation must never change any exit code, and Stop's exit 2 stays write-back-only.** — chose **`guard` as an optional companion field to `rule` on decision_logged — `path:`/`cmd:` domain-prefixed comma-separated globs (leading `!` exempts) evaluated by the fold against file_touched/command_run events logged AFTER that decision; violations are derived state surfaced as warnings only (doctor axis, UserPromptSubmit line, and the existing Stop block message)** over a hand-written .sofar/guards.json; regex predicates; blocking Stop on violation; deriving the predicate from the rule prose because the violation must name the decision, so the predicate belongs on the same event as the clause it enforces — a side file drifts from the rule it claims to guard. Same one-field-one-concept grain as D1, and `guard` REQUIRES `rule`: a guard with no clause has nothing to cite when it fires. Globs over regex — agent-authored patterns must be safe to compile and cheap inside the 100ms hook budget, and every ambiguity resolves to a non-match. `path:` anchors at a segment boundary so it matches the tail of the ABSOLUTE paths hooks log (portable across machines, which absolute matching is not); `cmd:` matches as a substring, because `cmd:npm publish` silently never firing would be a guard that reads as compliance. Non-retroactive — a guard only sees events after its own decision, or the first thing it flags is the work that motivated it. Warn, never block: Stop's one deliberate exit 2 stays write-back only (BD2/BD22), a false-positive block stops real work, and inferring intent to avoid false positives would need a model call (SPEC zero-model-API-calls).
